title: Price tag plus running cost
hook: A higher upfront price can cross a lower one after repeated running costs.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Combine an upfront amount and repeated operating charges without assuming the same winner at every horizon.

misconception: The lower initial price guarantees a lower total at every future horizon.
objective: Combine an upfront amount and repeated operating charges without assuming the same winner at every horizon.

claims.text: Illustrative A costs €80 plus 120kWh/year. B costs €140 plus 60kWh/year. Electricity is €0.30/kWh. Scaled model; illustrative:€80+120kWh/y;€140+60kWh/y;€0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Years=2, A=€152 and B=€176. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",80,["*",120,0.3,"x"]]; B=["+",140,["*",60,0.3,"x"]]; x denotes Years. At x=2, A=152, B=176; recall at x=5: B=230. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Add the upfront term to repeated running costs. A starts lower, while B’s modeled running cost grows more slowly. This arithmetic omits repair, lifespan and discounting and is not a purchasing recommendation.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff.

safety.assumptions: Illustrative A costs €80 plus 120kWh/year. B costs €140 plus 60kWh/year. Electricity is €0.30/kWh.
